cards.claim: Reducing Newton-Schulz iterations from Muon's 5-10 steps to a single iteration preserves correlation control while reducing computational overhead
cards.conditions: General optimization context; applies to matrix updates in neural networks
cards.effect: Reduced per-step cost with retained update quality; cheaper than Muon while maintaining some correlation suppression
cards.evidence: Design rationale and comparative method description
cards.quote: Compared to Muon's multi-step Newton-Schulz iterations (5-10 steps), AuON requires only one iteration, reducing overhead while retaining some correlation control.

cards.claim: Hybrid-AuON using single or few Newton-Schulz iterations (1, 3, or 5) followed by AuON rescaling offers middle ground: more stable than plain AuON, cheaper than Muon
cards.conditions: Training with spectral trust-region normalization; general deep learning
cards.effect: Computational savings versus Muon with improved stability versus plain AuON
cards.quote: We therefore introduce a hybrid scheme: apply a single Newton-Schulz iteration(Auon+) or 3(AuON+3) or 5(AuON+5) Newton-Schulz iterations to partially decorrelate the update, followed by AuON rescaling to enforce spectral contraction.

cards.claim: Hyperbolic cosine RMS scaling provides automatic tail-aware damping that suppresses exploding gradients without per-coordinate reweighting, enabling step-size management
cards.conditions: Optimization with heavy-tailed or spiky gradient updates; especially under attention-head instability
cards.effect: Automatic stabilization of training without manual intervention; automatically freezes unstable layers when gradients spike
cards.quote: This yields scale invariance with tail-aware damping, without introducing per-coordinate reweighting in the final update. As a result, as soon as attention logits start to explode (creating gradient spikes), AuON automatically suppresses the update to near-zero.

cards.claim: Muon's cubic computation complexity and susceptibility to exploding attention logits are limitations that AuON addresses via linear-time alternative with automatic emergency brake
cards.conditions: Large-scale Transformer training and other settings prone to attention instability; Muon baseline
cards.effect: Muon(Vanilla) suffers from exploding logits; AuON provides automatic stabilization mechanism absent in Muon
cards.evidence: Empirical observation and mechanism design comparison
cards.quote: Nevertheless, Muon(Vanilla) suffers from exploding attention logits and has cubic computation complexity. In this paper we deep dive into orthogonal momentum gradient updates to find the main properties that help Muon achieve remarkable performance. We propose AuON (Alternative Unit-norm momentum updates by Normalized nonlinear scaling), a linear-time optimizer that achieves strong performance without approximate orthogonal matrices, while preserving structural alignment and reconditioning ill-posed updates. AuON has an automatic ( "emergency brake" ) to handle exploding attention logits.

cards.claim: Hybrid-AuON with Newton-Schulz iterations outperforms Muon in language modeling tasks
cards.conditions: Language modeling; Hybrid-AuON versus Muon comparison
cards.effect: Better performance than Muon on LM benchmarks
cards.quote: We further introduce a hybrid variant ( Hybrid-AuON )that applies the linear transformations with Newton-Schulz iterations, which outperforms Muon in the language modeling tasks.

cards.claim: Cosh-based normalization acts as nonlinear stability sensor: nearly quadratic in safe regime (well-behaved gradients), exponentially sensitive to rare large-magnitude outliers (spikes)
cards.conditions: Gradient-based optimization with potential for heavy tails; large outliers from instability
cards.effect: Automatic sensitivity to instability without manual hyperparameter tuning; exponential suppression of spikes
cards.quote: The function exhibits two distinct asymptotic behaviors depending on the magnitude of the input gradient: 1. cards.claim: AuON's temperature-scaled variant with hyperparameter tau makes brake extremely sensitive to tensor width and heavy-tailed updates; smaller tau maintains more uniform braking across tensor shapes
cards.conditions: Temperature-scaled AuON variant; varying tensor sizes d; presence of heavy tails
cards.effect: Smaller tau: more uniform braking across layers; Larger tau: dramatic step reduction in wide layers; enables cross-layer behavior control
